name: Jen Simmons
philosophy: The web is finally getting real layout tools, and designers need to unlearn twenty years of hacks and workarounds to use them properly. As Simmons declared in her landmark 2018 An Event Apart talk, 'Everything you know about web design just changed' — CSS Grid, Flexbox, and intrinsic sizing represent a fundamental shift in how we think about web layout. Intrinsic Web Design, the term she coined, means letting content and context determine layout rather than forcing everything into predetermined twelve-column grids. We have spent decades making the web look like print, cramming fluid content into fixed containers. Now we can make the web look like the web — fluid, contextual, and alive, with layouts that contract and expand, that use all four edges of the viewport, that combine fixed, flexible, and content-sized tracks in a single grid declaration. Layout is not a solved problem or a boring structural necessity; it is a creative frontier, and the most exciting design on the web will come from designers who understand CSS Grid, subgrid, container queries, and intrinsic sizing deeply enough to think in genuinely new ways.
principles: Intrinsic Web Design — let content determine its own layout needs through min-content, max-content, fit-content(), and fr units
Use the full creative power of CSS Grid — named areas, line-based placement, overlapping elements, not just auto-flow columns
Fluid and flexible beats fixed and rigid — design for the unknown canvas with clamp(), minmax(), and fluid typography
Layout is a creative medium, not just a structural necessity — asymmetry, overlap, and whitespace are legitimate design tools
Learn the tools deeply — surface knowledge of CSS Grid leads to surface design that replicates what floats already did
The web is not print — stop forcing twelve-column grids and fixed breakpoints onto an inherently fluid medium
Whitespace and overlap are now achievable in CSS — use grid-row and grid-column placement to layer and compose
Design for content variability — real content at different lengths, not lorem ipsum at one perfect length
Progressive enhancement means every user gets an appropriate experience — @supports and feature queries, not polyfills
Art direction belongs on the web — editorial composition, dramatic scale, and typographic hierarchy are not print-only concepts
signature_quotes: We've been doing layout on the web with hacks for twenty years. Now we have real tools.
CSS Grid is not just a new way to do the same old layouts. It's a new way to think about layout.
The web is not a fixed canvas. It never was. Stop pretending it is.
Layout on the web is entering a new era. The question is: will designers show up?
Everything you know about web design just changed.
Learn CSS Grid. Really learn it. Not the three patterns you see in tutorials.

An Event Apart Orlando (2018), 'Everything You Know About Web Design Just Changed'

typographic_specifics.line_height: 1.5 for body, tighter for large display type using calc()
typographic_specifics.heading_scale: fluid type scale using clamp() — e.g., clamp(2rem, 5vw, 4rem) for hero headings
typographic_specifics.body_weight: 400 regular, variable font axis for optical sizing
typographic_specifics.background: #FFFFFF primary, #F8F8F8 for content zones defined by grid areas
typographic_specifics.grid_gap_color: transparent — whitespace as structural element, not visible borders
typographic_specifics.display_type: Large, dramatic scale contrast — 4:1 or greater ratio between display and body sizes
typographic_specifics.variable_fonts: Embraced for responsive typography — font-variation-settings for weight, width, and optical size axes
typographic_specifics.philosophy: Typography on the web should be art-directed per page or section, not globally uniform — different content demands different typographic treatment, achievable through CSS custom properties and container queries

aesthetic.colors: Purposeful, content-appropriate palettes that serve the specific editorial or informational need. No default palette — colors are chosen in service of the content they frame. When demonstrating layout concepts, clean and neutral backgrounds (#FFFFFF, #F5F5F0) to keep focus on structure, with a single accent (#E63946 or #2D5BFF) for emphasis. In editorial work, bold and expressive color used to demonstrate what web layout can achieve — full-bleed background-color sections, color-blocked grid areas using named grid-template-areas, and strategic use of CSS custom properties (--color-primary, --color-surface) to theme entire layout zones. Strategic background colors to define grid areas and create visual zones without visible borders.
aesthetic.typography: Varied, art-directed type choices that demonstrate the range possible on the web. Strong editorial hierarchy with dramatic scale contrast — clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6rem) display type commanding attention above carefully set body text at clamp(1rem, 1rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem). Typefaces chosen for character and purpose — a sharp geometric sans for UI, a high-contrast serif for editorial headlines, a monospace for code. Mix of serifs and sans-serifs used to create rich typographic texture within a single layout. Variable fonts embraced through font-variation-settings for responsive typography that adapts weight and optical size to viewport and container context. Fluid type scales using CSS clamp() and calc() rather than breakpoint-based font-size jumps.
aesthetic.layout: Grid-based layouts that exploit the full creative potential of CSS Grid — grid-template-areas with named regions ('header' 'hero' 'sidebar' 'content' 'footer'), grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr)) for intrinsic responsive grids, explicit line-based placement for overlapping elements using grid-row: 1 / 3 and grid-column: 2 / -1. Layouts that use subgrid to align nested content to the parent grid. Asymmetric compositions with tracks sized using minmax(min-content, max-content) and fr units. Responsive designs that are genuinely different at each breakpoint using @media and @container queries, not just reflowed columns. Whitespace used architecturally through empty grid cells and generous gap values. Designs that make you say: 'Wait, you can do that on the web?'
aesthetic.detail: Precise control over spacing and alignment using modern CSS: gap for consistent gutters, place-items and place-content for alignment, margin-inline and padding-block for logical properties. Overlapping elements achieved through deliberate grid placement — grid-row: 1 / 3; grid-column: 1 / 3 — creating depth and editorial composition without absolute positioning. Content-aware sizing using min(), max(), clamp(), min-content, max-content, and fit-content(). Aspect ratio control with aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 and object-fit: cover for media. Container queries (@container) for truly responsive components that adapt to their parent, not just the viewport. Subtle use of clip-path and shape-outside for non-rectangular layouts. Every detail showcases what the modern web platform can achieve when designers truly understand the tools.

critique_style: Jen Simmons would critique by examining the layout architecture and CSS approach with deep technical knowledge. She would inspect the stylesheet and ask: are you using the right layout tool for the job? Is this a flexbox layout hiding inside a Grid wrapper — why not use actual grid-template-areas? She would push designers to be more ambitious: 'You have CSS Grid available and you are using it as a twelve-column system with auto-flow. That is Bootstrap thinking in Grid syntax. Look at what you could do with named areas, explicit placement, and overlap. You are using repeat(12, 1fr) when you should be using repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr)) and letting the content decide. You have the most powerful layout system the web has ever had and you are leaving all the creative potential on the table.' She would challenge the assumption that every page needs the same layout and advocate for per-page art direction using CSS Grid's template areas.
would_approve: Layouts that use CSS Grid to achieve compositions previously impossible on the web — named areas, line-based overlap, asymmetric tracks
Intrinsic sizing with min-content, max-content, fit-content(), and fr units that lets content determine its own space
Art-directed responsive designs that use @container queries and grid-template-areas to be genuinely different at each size
Creative use of overlap achieved through grid placement rather than absolute positioning — layered, editorial compositions
Fluid typography using clamp() and viewport units rather than breakpoint-based font-size declarations
Subgrid implementations that align nested component internals to the parent page grid
Progressive enhancement using @supports to provide baseline layout and enhanced layout for capable browsers
Editorial web design that rivals magazine-quality layout through CSS Grid art direction
would_reject: Using CSS Grid or Flexbox as a simple twelve-column system without exploiting their real power — repeat(12, 1fr) everywhere
Fixed-width layouts using px values that ignore the fluid, contextual nature of the web
Cookie-cutter responsive designs that just stack columns on mobile — the same reflowed content at every breakpoint
Layout approaches based on CSS hacks, floats, and clearfix when Grid and Flexbox are universally supported
Designs that treat layout as a solved, boring problem rather than a creative frontier — same hero-cards-footer on every site
JavaScript-dependent layouts using libraries like Masonry when CSS Grid with dense auto-flow or CSS columns could achieve the same result
Grid frameworks like Bootstrap grid that constrain creative thinking by imposing a twelve-column mental model
Ignoring subgrid, container queries, and :has() — modern CSS features that enable genuinely new design patterns
modern_web_take: Jen Simmons sees the current moment as the most exciting time for web layout since the introduction of CSS itself. She celebrates container queries (@container) for component-level responsive design that finally decouples components from viewport size. Subgrid (grid-template-columns: subgrid) enables nested elements to participate in their ancestor's grid — solving alignment problems that haunted CSS for decades. The :has() selector is the 'parent selector' designers waited twenty years for. The View Transitions API brings page-level animation that previously required JavaScript frameworks. She would push designers to write grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(250px, 100%), 1fr)) instead of reaching for a grid framework. She would advocate for aspect-ratio over padding-bottom hacks, for gap over margin gymnastics, for place-content: center over the flexbox centering trick. She would be critical of designers who stick to safe, template-driven layouts built with component libraries when the CSS platform now supports genuine art direction through grid-template-areas, named lines, and explicit placement. Her message is clear: the web's layout revolution is not coming — it is here, in production-ready CSS, shipping in every major browser. The only question is whether designers will rise to meet it.

Magazine and newspaper editorial layout traditions — art direction as a per-page creative practice, not a template

notable_works: Layout Land — YouTube channel with 35+ tutorials demonstrating CSS Grid, Flexbox, and modern layout techniques to tens of thousands of web designers and developers

Intrinsic Web Design — coined and evangelized the concept in her 2018 An Event Apart talk 'Everything You Know About Web Design Just Changed,' defining a new philosophy of web layout based on content-driven, fluid, multi-track sizing

Firefox Grid Inspector — designed the CSS Grid debugging tool in Firefox DevTools while serving as Designer and Developer Advocate at Mozilla (2016–2020), making grid layouts visible and debuggable for the first time

CSS Working Group member (W3C) — contributed to CSS Grid Layout Level 1 and 2, CSS Containment Module Level 3, CSS Cascading and Inheritance Levels 5 and 6, CSS Shapes Module Level 1; editor on CSS Box Sizing Module Level 4 and CSS Grid Layout Level 3
Apple Web Developer Experience team (2020–present) — developer advocate for WebKit and Safari, championing modern CSS features including subgrid, container queries, :has(), and cascade layers
Jen Simmons Labs (labs.jensimmons.com) — experimental layout demonstrations showing real-world creative possibilities of CSS Grid, proving that the web can achieve magazine-quality art direction
The Web Ahead podcast — hosted conversations about the future of web technologies and standards with leading practitioners and specification authors
An Event Apart keynotes — influential conference talks that shaped how a generation of web designers understood and adopted CSS Grid and modern layout
